description: Shared source of truth for the search-result merge rules that the frontend
MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SOURCES ceiling, the MAX_SOURCE_ADDRS cap, and the fields both
sides resolve by keeping the first non-empty value.
src/lib/stores/search.ts merges streamed batches per tab, src-tauri/src/search/merge.rs
merges the lists it emits, and the two were kept aligned only by a comment.
Checked by scripts/merge-contract.test.mjs and by the fixture tests in merge.rs.
Only rules that MUST agree belong here. The deliberate divergences are out of
scope on purpose: Rust sums availability across ed2k-only origins while the
frontend takes the max (the backend already summed within a network), Rust
elects the filename by vote while the frontend keeps the first name it saw,
Origin cases stay within the ASCII origin labels: the two sides agree on
ordering there (JS sorts by UTF-16 code unit, Rust by byte).

result_key_cases.name: the ed2k hash wins over every fallback
a pending id outranks the path when there is no hash
the path is used when the id is not a pending row
name and size identify a row with no hash, id or path
an empty name and a zero size still produce a stable key
sizes above 32 bits are not truncated or exponentiated

note: Fields both merges resolve by keeping the first non-empty value. They are
inline expressions rather than named functions, so they cannot be lifted and
run the way resultKey and pickEmberDigest are; the test asserts the shape of
each side instead, which is the same technique the MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SOURCES
clamp check uses. Listed because file_type, rating and comment silently
resolved in OPPOSITE directions for a long time -- Rust kept the existing
value, the store took the incoming one -- so the same two rows merged
differently depending on which layer merged them.
aich_hash is here because it is a recovery hash a download consumes, it sits
one line from ember_file_hash (which has its own rule and its own cases), and
nothing but a comment on each side held the two together.

ember_digest_cases.name: an empty row takes the digest the network offered
a row with a digest keeps it when the other side has none
a later Ember batch replaces an earlier slice-local plurality
the library's own digest outranks a network claim
a row the library already contributed to is still protected
a KAD row that somehow carries one is treated like any other claim
nothing on either side stays empty
